metadata.title: A Width-Chain Estimate of the MOND Acceleration Scale from MIGHTEE-HI COSMOS, with its Flux-Scale, Line-Width and Kernel Systematics
metadata.description:
Version 1.1 (draft for review; not peer reviewed). Version 1.0 read the catalogue line widths as observed-frame and divided them by 1+z; the catalogue paper's own worked examples show they are rest-frame (referee lane CFG306, confirmed by the frozen lane CFG309), so version 1.1 makes the rest-frame reading primary and also replaces the flux-scale range, adds the kernel, width-side and selection systematics, and corrects the description of prior work.

The programme ties MOND's acceleration scale to the vacuum, a0 = kappa c sqrt(G rho_Lambda), with kappa = 1/2 fitted, not derived; its footings are 9.3603e-11 (rho_Lambda) and 1.1312e-10 m s^-2 (rho_crit). We apply a width chain, frozen before any width was read, to the MeerKAT MIGHTEE-HI COSMOS catalogue: V comes from the rest-frame W50 and optical inclination, the baryons are 1.33 M_HI + M* at half the HI diameter, and a median-residual estimator with the exponential kernel returns a0. Forty-seven golden discs at 0.027 <= z <= 0.093 survive, all at g_bar/a0 <= 0.084, 37 gas-dominated.

Result. On the catalogue's flux scale a0 = 1.31e-10 m s^-2 (statistical +-0.034 dex, recipe +-0.128 dex), kappa = 0.70 or 0.58: consistent with SPARC and the alternative footing, the canonical footing just outside the recipe width. Arecibo fluxes exceed the catalogue's for brighter, nearer galaxies; applied to our discs' gas, a0 falls to 1.07 (0.97-1.13)e-10, inside the recipe width of both footings. Line-width corrections lower a0 by up to 0.10 dex; kernels without the exponential's next-order term raise it by 0.06-0.07 dex. A SPARC closure tests only the baryon recipe. The width frame rests on the catalogue paper's worked examples; independent data tests could not decide it.

What it can and cannot say. The result is not a footing discriminator and, with a lever of 0.009 dex, not an a0(z) test. The cold mass (Omega_c h^2 ~ 0.12) is still required; no dark-matter particle is added; nothing here says the data favour the framework.

Every number carried by an audit row is re-read from committed files by PAPER40_audit.py (375 of 375; 19 literature values are checked only for being printed; 236 plain numbers are also found in the PDF text); the post hoc rows come from make_paper40_figures.py, which first reproduces the lanes' committed values exactly. AI-assisted research programme; not peer reviewed.
